deliverables.title: Stage 1 — a recording to a speaker-attributed transcript

threads.title: Transcription (four typists: faster-whisper large-v3 and others)
threads.question: Turns the waveform into words. Four candidates are staged and one has been the default, which is not a decision.

tasks.text: Add a duration check to the 1a seam: check_segment_contract takes the audio duration and fails a typist whose last segment ends far short of it
Canary transcribes only the first 17.8 s of a session. Chunked inference would fix it, if canary is worth that work

decisions.q: Is canary-1b-flash worth chunked inference, given parakeet already covers the NVIDIA design

decisions.rule: Discarded. Keeping them would confound the typist axis with the alignment axis, the one thing the grid exists to separate.

threads.title: Word alignment (wav2vec2 base, LibriSpeech)
threads.question: Puts a start and an end on every word. The least examined stage: a small model trained on read audiobooks, never compared, while therapy speech is spontaneous and overlapped.

tasks.text: Build the reference RTTM: re-align the reference transcript's words to the audio and write measured word times. The job reads the reference locally and prints counts only
Then compare two aligners on the same words: the large wav2vec2 bundle, or one built for forced alignment, against the current one

threads.title: Diarization (five arms: pyannote, Sortformer, DiariZen)
threads.question: Says who was speaking when, reading no words at all. Five arms, compared, still undecided.

decisions.rule: RTTM. The join reads exactly start, end and speaker, and the file the join reads is the file a scorer consumes.

threads.title: The speaker join (Stage 1c)
threads.question: Lays the turn table over the timed words, so every word knows who said it, and renders the readable transcript.

decisions.rule: 1a, then 1b with community-1, then 1c reproduces job 2032471 exactly: 489 segments, 7298 words, 2 speakers, 89 turns, 1 UNKNOWN segment. Any deviation is a bug in the split.

threads.title: The reference transcript (a human-adjudicated artifact)
threads.question: colibri built it from the community-1 baseline and the annotator's error log, and she approved it. It lives under phi/, outside git, and nothing in psych_asr builds, reads or reproduces it.

decisions.rule: The annotator's approved transcript, because she says it is. The correction algorithm, error-log reader, grader and scorers are deleted: placing her corrections turned out to be judgement, not code.

threads.title: Measuring an arm against the reference
threads.question: How is one transcription-alignment-diarization combination measured against the reference? Nothing is built until that is decided, and the answer may not be code.

decisions.q: How an arm is measured against the reference transcript

threads.title: The grid sweep (4 typists x 2 aligners x 5 diarizers)
threads.question: A cube, not a table: 40 cells from 13 jobs, because diarization reads no words and so depends on neither other axis.

tasks.text: Build: widen run_typist_bakeoff.sh's driver to two aligners, 8 runs of 1a beside 5 of 1b, and join every cell that lands. Every grid-aware caller passes --stem

decisions.rule: 13 jobs, never 40: one 1a run per typist and aligner pair, one 1b run per diarizer, and the cells assembled afterwards. Diarization is never rerun per typist.

threads.title: Choosing the combination for the remaining sessions
threads.question: Reads the whole grid and says which combination is worth running on the rest of the sessions.

threads.title: Reviewing a diarized recording by ear
threads.question: Does the diarized transcript match who is speaking when the recording is played? Only a person listening can say.

tasks.text: The owner's own: listen to the recording beside its diarized transcript
